bibliography.checked_against: Crossref and the article's first page
bibliography.note: Glenn A. Benoy and Jacob Kalff, 'Sediment accumulation and Pb burdens in submerged macrophyte beds', Limnol. Oceanogr. 44(4), 1999, 1081–1090. The entry agrees.

claims.claim: plant beds accumulate 2–20 times more sediment than open bottom (Benoy & Kalff 1999)
claims.source_value: 2 to 20 times more per m² than the PROFUNDAL (deep-water) zone, not than open (unvegetated) littoral bottom: macrophyte-bed bulk sediment accumulation rates (Pb-dated, ~110 yr) against published inorganic rates of 15–78 g m⁻² yr⁻¹ for profundal Lake Memphremagog (Rowan et al. 1992)
claims.location: p. 1081 (PDF p. 1), abstract; p. 1089 (PDF p. 9), Discussion; Table 2, p. 1085 (PDF p. 5)
claims.quote: rates 2 to 20 times greater (per m2) than in the profundal zone
claims.conditions: 30 macrophyte-bed sites in Lake Memphremagog (Quebec–Vermont), three cores taken per site and the longest analysed (all three at 5 sites), sediment dated by the stable-Pb horizon (~110 yr); bulk SAR (dry weight, mostly inorganic) mean 743.8 g m⁻² yr⁻¹, range 38.8–1,669.8 over 29 sites (Table 2, read on the page image); total SAR mean 1.7 mm yr⁻¹; 4 of the 30 sites had no appreciable accumulation, and littoral sites steeper than about 10 % or more exposed than about 10 km² cannot accumulate sediment at all
claims.note: The digits are right but the comparison is beds versus deep-water bottom. Unvegetated littoral bottom was not measured; on steep or exposed shores it accumulates nothing, so 'than the deep-water (profundal) bottom' is the faithful wording. The rates scale with plant biomass density (best predictor of total and organic SAR).

tried.note: Wiley bot check (OpenAlex lists this free 'bronze' PDF)

notes: Other values: anthropogenic Pb burdens in the littoral beds averaged almost 4.5 times the profundal burdens of nine Eastern Townships lakes (p. 1089); peak Pb 115 vs background 31 µg/g; organic SAR mean 83.1 g m⁻² yr⁻¹; biomass density, then mean biomass, best predicted total and organic SAR, while slope and exposure mattered mainly at the extremes. The study sites had exposures up to 25.4 km² (Table 2), so the exposure thresholds do not transfer to the small Hot Brook lakes, but the plant-density effect may.
